### Devotional: Numbers 36
Author: D. A. Carson
Site: The Gospel Coalition
URL: https://www.thegospelcoalition.org/devotionals/read-the-bible/numbers-36-psalm-80-isaiah-28-2-john/
Passage: Numbers 36:1-13
Points:
- Manasseh’s clan leaders raised concerns that tribal property would transfer permanently to other tribes if Zelophehad's daughters married outside their tribe.
- The Lord affirmed the concern and commanded that female heirs must marry within their father's tribal clan to protect tribal boundaries.
- The daughters of Zelophehad readily complied with God's ruling by marrying cousins within the clan of Manasseh.
- Modern Western culture tends to idolize personal romance and radical individualism at the expense of family and covenant community.
- Believers are called to submit their personal desires to God's design rather than expecting God's universe to revolve around their preferences.

### 3 Important Lessons from the Daughters of Zelophehad
Author: Mike Leake
Site: Crosswalk
URL: https://www.crosswalk.com/faith/bible-study/lessons-from-the-daughters-of-zelophehad.html
Passage: Numbers 36:1-13
Points:
- The case of Zelophehad’s daughters addressed the unintended consequence of tribal property transferring to other tribes through marriage.
- God demonstrated His attentiveness to vulnerable people by providing a fair and practical legal solution.
- The Lord’s statutes were designed for human flourishing and relation with Him rather than cold, robotic legalism.
- The temporary earthly allotment secured by the sisters points to the eternal, unfading inheritance believers possess in Jesus Christ.
